1.note: The word **Qoheleth** is the name that the main speaker of this book chose to use for himself. In the original language it is a title that means “one who assembles a group,” that is, someone who gathers people together in order to teach them. You could spell out how this name sounds in your language, as the ULT does, or you could translate its meaning, as the UST does with “the Teacher.”

2.note: Qoheleth is using **Vapor of vapors** as a common expression of his culture to mean “the most fleeting thing of all.” In this expression, a word is repeated in the possessive form in order to express a superlative. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [The most fleeting thing of all] or [Utterly temporary]

Qoheleth says **the whole** as an extreme statement for emphasis. He does not mean that every single thing without exception is fleeting. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [just about everything is vapor]

3.q: מַה יִּתְר֖וֹן לָֽ⁠אָדָ֑ם בְּ⁠כָל עֲמָל֔⁠וֹ שֶֽׁ⁠יַּעֲמֹ֖ל תַּ֥חַת הַ⁠שָּֽׁמֶשׁ
3.note: Qoheleth is not using the question form to emphasize that people gain nothing lasting from all their labor. Instead, this is a genuine question. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [I wonder if there is any profit for a human in exchange for all his toil that he toils under the sun!]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **profit**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [good thing that lasts]

Qoheleth is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this.

Qoheleth is using **under the sun** as a common expression of his culture to mean “in this life on the earth.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. See the Introduction to Ecclesiastes for more information on translating this expression here and throughout this chapter. Alternate translation: [in this earthly life]

4.note: Qoheleth is referring to the whole cycle of human life by naming its two major components, one generation **going** and another generation **coming**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [People are continually dying and being born]

5.note: Qoheleth is speaking of the sun as if it were a living thing that could be **panting** as it hurried back to the place where it rises. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [it goes back quickly to rise there again]

6.note: Qoheleth is referring to all directions by naming two major components, **south** and **north**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in every direction]

6.q: הוֹלֵ֣ךְ הָ⁠ר֔וּחַ וְ⁠עַל סְבִיבֹתָ֖י⁠ו שָׁ֥ב הָ⁠רֽוּחַ
6.note: Qoheleth is speaking of **the wind** as if it were a living thing that could choose where to travel and then decide to return the same way. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the wind simply blows around and around in the same course]

8.note: The expression **is not filled** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and an ear does not fill up]

Qoheleth says **All the things are wearisome** and **a person is not able to speak** as extreme statements for emphasis. He means that the endless repetition he has been describing is exhausting to consider and that no one could ever finish describing how wearisome these things are. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [Very many things indeed are wearisome; a person could never finish describing them]

Qoheleth is not referring to a specific **person**. He means people in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [anyone]

8.q: לֹא תִשְׂבַּ֥ע עַ֨יִן֙ לִ⁠רְא֔וֹת וְ⁠לֹא תִמָּלֵ֥א אֹ֖זֶן מִ⁠שְּׁמֹֽעַ
8.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [People are never satisfied by anything they see or hear]

9.note: The expressions **has been done** and **will be done** are passive verbal forms. If it would be unnatural to use those forms, you could express the ideas in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and whatever people have done, it that which people will do]
See how you translated the same expression in 1:3.

10.q: יֵ֥שׁ דָּבָ֛ר שֶׁ⁠יֹּאמַ֥ר רְאֵה זֶ֖ה חָדָ֣שׁ ה֑וּא
10.note: Qoheleth is using the question form to make an emphatic statement, that nothing anyone points to is actually new. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [There is nothing about which one says, “See this, it is new!”]
The pronoun **one** refers to any person at all, not to a specific individual. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [about which anyone says]
If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [that this thing is something new]

Here, **our faces** represents “us,” that is, the people who are alive now. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from before us]

11.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **memory**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [anyone remembering]

Qoheleth is referring to people and events of every time by naming two major components, **the former times** and **the latter times**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the people and events of every time]

13.note: The expression **is done** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [all that people are doing]

Qoheleth is using **I gave my heart** as a common expression of his culture to mean “I devoted my mind.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [So, I set my mind]

The terms **to seek** and **to explore** mean similar things. Qoheleth is using the two terms together for emphasis, indicating that his investigation was thorough. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [to search out thoroughly]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **wisdom**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [wisely]

Qoheleth is using **under the heavens** as a common expression of his culture to mean “in this life on the earth.” This expression means the same thing as “under the sun” in 1:3. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [during this earthly life]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **business**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [something unpleasant that]

Qoheleth is using **the sons of humanity** as a common expression of his culture to mean “human beings.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to human beings]

14.note: Qoheleth is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation here and in verse 16. Alternate translation: [and—pay attention]

Qoheleth is speaking of everything people do as if it were a **pursuit of wind**. He means that gaining anything lasting from these deeds is as futile as trying to catch the wind. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and as futile as trying to catch the wind]

15.note: Qoheleth is speaking of what is wrong in the world as if it were a **bent** object that someone might try to make straight. He means that people cannot correct the things that are wrong with life. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [What is wrong in life—no one is able to make it right]

16.note: See how you translated the phrase **my heart** in 1:13

The word **saying** introduces the words that Qoheleth spoke to himself. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this term explicitly.

Here, **my face** represents Qoheleth speaking of himself. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before me in Jerusalem]

Qoheleth is speaking of his **heart** as if it were a person who could see. In this culture, the heart represented a person’s thoughts and understanding, and seeing something represented experiencing and knowing it. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and in my thinking I have experienced much wisdom and knowledge]

The terms **wisdom** and **knowledge** mean similar things. Qoheleth is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [wise understanding]

17.note: See how you translated the same expression in 1:13.

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **wisdom**, **madness**, and **folly**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [what is sound judgment and what is poor judgment]
See how you translated the same expression in 1:14.

18.q: בְּ⁠רֹ֥ב חָכְמָ֖ה רָב כָּ֑עַס וְ⁠יוֹסִ֥יף דַּ֖עַת יוֹסִ֥יף מַכְאֽוֹב
18.note: If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **wisdom**, **anger**, **knowledge**, and **pain**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [For in much wise thinking is much angry feeling, and when one increases the things he knows, he increases the things that hurt him]
